chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: The Negro Actors Guild charges against his second wife
summary: His wife, an executive of the Guild, was accused over missing funds; he believes it a set-up, sent her back from San Francisco, and kept the apartment during her prison term.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: The trouble I had to get back to America. The trouble that she had in the incident that happened concerning the Guild, she was executive of a Guild -- Negro Actors Guild. She was executive of that Guild at the time and some funds got misappropriated and she was found to be guilty of it and I know it was a set up because one of the guys, his safe was busted and he had to get a safe man to unlock the safe and he fixed it so she wouldn't be able to get the safe open and he took some things -- fixed it so she couldn't get the safe open and he took some things that she would be accused of out of the safe so she wouldn't get to open it until she got the safe man to open the safe, and at the same time she was going to take a vacation and come to California with me, joining the theater with Paul Small and Finklehoff, Ella Logan's husband and an agent friend of his in "Curtain Time" and "Laugh Time" at the Current Theater in San Francisco.

So she came and I asked her, did she have everything straight, she said yes. She hadn't been in San Francisco one week before the news was out and they were looking for her. So when I got the wind of it, I talked her into going back to New York -- don't let them pick her up here. Go back to New York, it's better for you.

So I sent her back to New York and when she left the club to go back to New York that's when the detectives came to the club to find her with me, but she had gone. But I still don't believe at that time that she's guilty of nothing.

However, that went down and she got back to New York, then this fella, he's alive yet, the guy that said everything was going to be all right, he was going to help her and take care of her. He was the one that held her like, I got the crook here, I got the thief here, instead of telling her what best to do. And he's an old-timer.
So she serves her time and after she finishes -- I waited, kept the apartment so she'd have some place to come to and stood by her. Her daughter was going to be a mother, she had the child.
